turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: My skin keeps getting sores that sometimes have pus, and I’ve had lots of fevers and colds. I also seem to have swollen bumps in my neck, and I’m not growing as well as other kids.
I’m sorry you’re dealing with that. One question to start: **how old is the patient, and when did these symptoms begin?**
Patient: I’m 3 years old, and the skin sores started when I was about 2 months. The fevers and colds have been coming back since then too.
Thanks. Next question: **Do the skin sores tend to be in specific areas (e.g., around the mouth, armpits/groin, diaper area), or are they scattered anywhere on the body?**

They’re kind of scattered all over my skin, but I notice them on and off in spots like my armpits and groin too, and sometimes near where the diaper rubs. Some of them are different sizes, and a few leak pus.
Next question: **Have any of the sores left scars, or do they heal slowly (taking more than ~2 weeks), or do they keep coming back in the same places?**
They’ve left some marks on my skin, and they seem to take a while to heal—sometimes longer than two weeks. They also keep coming back in different spots, not just one exact place.
Next question: **Have you noticed any mouth sores, diarrhea, or trouble swallowing—or is it mainly skin infections plus fevers/colds?**
Patient: I haven’t had sores in my mouth, and I don’t have diarrhea or trouble swallowing—it's mostly the skin sores, my fevers, and lots of colds.
Next question: **When you say “swollen bumps in my neck,” do they feel like lymph nodes (movable lumps under the skin), and are they tender or painless?**
They feel like movable lumps under my skin in my neck, and I think they can be a bit tender. They don’t stay in just one spot—they seem to come and go.
Next question: **Has the child had any blood test results you know of—especially low white blood cells, low platelets, or anemia?**

Patient: I don’t know the exact blood test results, but my caregiver says the doctors have mentioned concerns because I keep getting infections and my growth hasn’t been so good. I haven’t been told that I have low white blood cells or low platelets specifically.
Next question: **Have any doctors ever mentioned “granulomas,” “catalase test,” or “chronic granulomatous disease,” or have you had any imaging/biopsies of the skin lesions?**

Doctor: Have any doctors ever mentioned “granulomas,” “catalase test,” or “chronic granulomatous disease,” or have you had any imaging or biopsies of the skin lesions? Patient: I don’t remember those names, but the sores have been checked by doctors and I’ve had treatments, and they keep coming back. I don’t think I had any biopsy.
Next question: **What treatments have been tried for the skin sores (for example antibiotics like TMP-SMX/cephalexin, antifungals, or steroid creams), and did any of them clearly help?**

Patient: They tried antibiotics a few times when the sores looked infected, and sometimes other creams, but the sores keep coming back. I’m not sure about the exact names, and I think nothing made them go away for good.
Next question: **Do the fevers happen with the skin flares (at the same time), or do they come independently of the sores?**
Patient: The fevers usually come around the time my skin sores flare up, and then I also get more colds while that’s happening. They don’t seem totally separate from the skin problems.
Next question: **Any history of severe infections like pneumonia, deep abscesses, or infections with unusual organisms (e.g., fungal infections), or is it mostly skin + typical colds?**

Patient: I’ve had several respiratory infections like colds that keep coming back, but I don’t know about pneumonia. I get skin abscess-like sores that sometimes drain pus, and doctors have said the infections keep returning. I haven’t been told about any unusual fungal infections.
